gates.evidence: Versioned threat model covers the exact six source trust zones—trusted host, guest JS, package bytes, preview edge, storage and future AI credentials—with controls/evidence paths validated by the technical court.
OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 is frozen by official asset SHA-256 and mapped only to requirements relevant to the deployed browser-native architecture; the mapping explicitly retains human review.

Shipping topology now enforces document CSP, Permissions-Policy, COOP/COEP/CORP, nosniff and no-referrer plus separate strict/toolchain Worker CSPs; hosting self-check and Chrome product path validate the controls.

Capability review exercises external/LNA network policy, redirect reauthorization, opaque secret binding, lifecycle-script denial and persistence authority boundaries; guest capability membrane remains deny-by-default.

Deterministic adversarial/fuzz courts cover path, URL/capability, exports/imports, lockfile, graph, TAR, diagnostic journal, snapshot/import and RPC-envelope parsers with fail-closed outcomes and publication invariants.

Workspace VFS, package archive/resolver, symlink canonicalization and snapshot/import courts reject traversal, duplicate canonical paths, special archive links and package-root escapes before canonical publication.

Resource-DoS review covers worker explosion, output floods, decompression, source maps and WASM memory growth. Source-map/WASM heap ceilings remain explicit residual risks and do not close P7/P15 device-floor evidence.
Service Worker install/activate/claim remains compatibility-authorized rather than unconditional; stale publication routes fail closed and release compatibility regressions are retained.

Preview edge strips host credentials, binds owner/epoch/workspace/session/version identity, rejects stale/tampered routes and exercises sandboxed hostile preview content in the declared Chrome profile.
OPFS/Web Locks and stale-generation courts treat multi-tab stale writers/split brain as security/data-integrity failures; old writers cannot publish over the current generation.

Generated secret sentinels are exercised across errors, diagnostics, support bundles, signed URLs, request/response bodies, source fields and provider/network paths with no retained plaintext leakage.
Commit-bound npm audit includes release dependencies and dev/build tooling; CI #409 reported zero info/low/moderate/high/critical vulnerabilities and zero blocking findings.
Pinned GitHub CodeQL v4.38.2 produced retained SARIF plus a commit-bound severity/waiver receipt; CI #409 reported 0 findings, 0 waivers and 0 unwaived high/critical blockers.

The frozen malicious-package corpus executes 11 negative cases covering traversal, absolute/backslash paths, links/special entries, duplicates, decompression expansion, lifecycle scripts, identity/integrity mismatch and redirect escape.
Registry-driven regression court re-executes every retained fixed critical/high issue: 12 registry entries across 11 executable test files passed and the raw regression log is SHA-256 bound.
Versioned security policy defines CRITICAL/HIGH/MODERATE/LOW acknowledgement/remediation SLA and makes CRITICAL/HIGH release-blocking; scanner scores cannot override release policy.
SECURITY.md documents supported-version policy, but no verified private/responsible-disclosure channel exists yet. Documentation alone cannot satisfy this gate.
No independent or second-party reviewer/review artifact has yet covered critical isolation/storage/network changes; machine/AI review is intentionally insufficient.

Versioned residual-risk register records browser-visible credential risk, toolchain unsafe-eval, single-profile evidence, weak-device gap, CDN/header dependency, third-party code, future AI credentials, broker SSRF and manual-review limits.
Policy explicitly forbids treating CodeQL/npm/CI/AI scores as a product-security claim, but the required human product-security review artifact has not yet been completed.

boundaries: This is a technical product-security review for the declared Chrome 153 / Ubuntu 24.04 x64 profile; it is not a claim that the product is secure.
P12-17 remains open until a verified private/responsible-disclosure channel exists.
P12-18 remains open until an independent or second-party review artifact covers critical isolation/storage/network changes.
P12-20 remains open until a human product-security review is completed; scanner, CI and AI evidence cannot substitute for it.
Source-map/WASM memory residual risks do not close P7 weak-device, long-run, memory-pressure or performance-floor gates.
This is not cross-browser, Windows, macOS, mobile, final-CDN/topology, legal/FTO or operations closure.
